references.text: The showbread that was to lie on the table in the tabernacle is described here as part of the sanctuary's furnishings.
Unleavened bread made from fine wheat flour (solet) is also used in the consecration ceremony for the priests.
Fine flour (solet) is also used in the grain offering, showing the use of the same ingredient in holy offerings.
Two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour are mentioned as a grain offering on the Sabbath, the same measure as for each of the showbread loaves.
Solomon made the table for the showbread for the temple, continuing the tradition of the twelve loaves.
The Levites were responsible for baking the showbread every Sabbath, as described in Leviticus 24.
The priests were responsible for the showbread and the fine flour, confirming the arrangement from 3 Mosebok.
Jesus refers to David eating the showbread, showing that these loaves were known in New Testament times.
Hebrews mentions the table with the showbread as part of the holy place in the tabernacle.
